newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hotung upbeat on Taiwan's high tech sector.
newsitem.headline: Hotung upbeat on Taiwan's high tech sector.

text.p: Hotung Investment Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was upbeat about the high technology sector in Taiwan and would continue to focus its investments there.
"Today, nobody can escape high-tech. High tech is everybody's industry," Hotung president Hong Shing Cheng told a news conference.

"Taiwan has a very strong commercial market for high-tech ideas," he said, adding that Taiwan held key market shares in many technological areas, including printed circuit boards, semiconductors, consumer electronics and telecommunications.
Hotung, a Taiwan-based venture capital investment group, launched its Singapore initial public offer of 242.4 million shares at US$0.26 each on Monday.
Besides three venture capital funds which invest in unlisted companies, it also owns 40 percent of an investment manager, Hotung International Company Ltd.
About 82 percent of the group's investments are in Taiwan's high-tech industries.

Hotung plans to use US$25 million from its IPO proceeds to set up a new fund to be incorporated in the British Virgin Islands. At least 50 percent of the new fund would go to high tech investments and mostly in Taiwan, Hong said.

Hotung is also taking the first steps towards becoming an investment bank. It plans to use US$13 million from the IPO to buy a 51 percent stake in a securities underwiting and investment trust business.

Hong said 11 companies are expected to list on the Taiwan Stock Exchange, including the over the counter trade market, in 1997. The number is expected to rise in the coming years, making securities underwriting a lucrative business.
The company's prospectus said Hotung expected to get its underwriting licence by the first quarter of 1998 and to incorporate the investment trust company by the third quarter of 1998.
On its venture capital business, Hotung is looking at placing management teams in Singapore, Philippines and Indonesia, Hong said.

In the next two years, Hotung is targetting a dividend yield of seven percent per annum based on its IPO price, said Dafney Phua, Peregrine Capital Ltd's director of International Equity Offerings Group.
